posts.post_title: Species That Ovulate Primary Oocytes
posts.post_content: In all domestic animals, ovulation occurs in the secondary oocyte stage, while in which species does ovulation occur in the primary oocyte stage?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Bitch and Mare

Among domestic animals, the bitch (dog) and the mare (horse) are unique in that they ovulate primary oocytes — all other domestic animals ovulate secondary oocytes.

Oocyte Maturation Stages
  • Primary oocyte: arrested in prophase I of meiosis — not yet undergone first meiotic division.
  • Secondary oocyte: after first meiotic division — ready for fertilization; arrested in metaphase II.
  • Mature ovum (ootid): after second meiotic division — only completes when fertilized by a sperm.
Bitch and Mare — Consequences of Primary Oocyte Ovulation
  • After ovulation, the primary oocyte must complete first meiotic division (takes 2–3 days in bitch) before fertilization can occur.
  • This accounts for the long fertile lifespans of sperm (4–6 days) and ova (4–8 days) in the bitch.
  • In the mare, the oocyte completes first meiotic division shortly after ovulation in the oviduct.

posts.post_title: Thawing Temperature for Frozen Semen
posts.post_content: Thawing temperature for frozen semen is:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 37–40°C for 30 seconds

Standard protocol for thawing frozen bull semen is to immerse the straw in a water bath at 37–40°C for 30 seconds. This rapid thaw minimizes re-crystallization injury to spermatozoa.

Why Rapid Thawing is Important
  • Slow thawing at room temperature allows ice crystals to reform inside sperm cells (recrystallization), causing cell membrane rupture and death.
  • Rapid thawing at 37–40°C quickly melts ice crystals before they can cause significant damage.
Post-Thaw Quality Parameters (Bull Semen)
  • Post-thaw motility should be ≥ 40%
  • Normal morphology ≥ 80%
  • Insemination should be done within 15 minutes of thawing for best conception rates.

posts.post_title: Minimum Normal Morphology in Bull Semen
posts.post_content: Morphologically normal sperm in bull semen should be at least:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 80%

For bull semen to be considered satisfactory for use in artificial insemination, at least 80% of spermatozoa must be morphologically normal. Semen with more than 20% abnormal sperm is considered unsatisfactory for AI use.

Sperm Morphology Terminology
  • Teratozoospermia: Abnormal sperm morphology (>20% abnormal)
  • Necrozoospermia: Dead spermatozoa in semen
  • Asthenozoospermia: Decreased sperm motility
  • Oligozoospermia: Reduced sperm concentration
  • Azoospermia: Complete absence of sperm in semen
Primary vs. Secondary Abnormalities
  • Primary (major) abnormalities: Arise during spermatogenesis in the testis — e.g., double heads, no tail, coiled midpiece. These are more detrimental to fertility.
  • Secondary (minor) abnormalities: Arise during epididymal transit — e.g., bent tail, detached heads, cytoplasmic droplets. Less impact on fertility.

posts.post_title: Number of Primary Spermatocytes from One Spermatogonium
posts.post_content: How many primary spermatocytes are produced from one spermatogonium?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 16

One spermatogonium undergoes 4 successive mitotic divisions (2⁴ = 16) to produce 16 primary spermatocytes. These primary spermatocytes then undergo meiosis to produce 64 spermatozoa.

Complete Spermatogenesis Cascade from 1 Spermatogonium
  • 1 Spermatogonium → (4 mitoses) → 16 Primary spermatocytes
  • 16 Primary spermatocytes → (Meiosis I) → 32 Secondary spermatocytes
  • 32 Secondary spermatocytes → (Meiosis II) → 64 Spermatids
  • 64 Spermatids → (Spermiogenesis) → 64 Spermatozoa
Key Numbers to Remember
  • 1 Spermatogonium → 16 primary spermatocytes → 64 sperm
  • 1 Primary spermatocyte → 4 sperm
  • 1 Primary oocyte → 1 ovum

posts.post_title: Trimester of Abortion Caused by Trichomonas foetus in Cattle
posts.post_content: Trichomonas foetus causes abortion in cattle during which trimester of pregnancy?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 1st trimester

Tritrichomonas foetus (a protozoan parasite) causes abortion in cattle specifically during the first trimester of pregnancy (first 3 months / approximately first 90 days).

Trichomoniasis in Cattle — Key Facts
  • It is a venereal disease — transmitted during coitus from infected bull to cow.
  • The organism colonizes the cervix and uterus, causing post-coital pyometra (uterus fills with a 'potato soup-like' pus).
  • Infection leads to early embryonic death and first-trimester abortion — hence repeat breeding is a common presentation.
  • Bulls are asymptomatic carriers; the organism lives in the penile sheath and prepuce.
Comparison of Trimester of Abortion by Pathogen
  • 1st trimester: Tritrichomonas foetus ✔
  • Last trimester: Brucella abortus, Leptospira, Listeria, Mycobacterium
Why Other Options Are Wrong
  • 2nd/3rd trimester → T. foetus primarily kills the embryo early; by the 2nd trimester the infection may lead to pyometra rather than abortion per se.

posts.post_title: Spontaneous Ovulator – Identification
posts.post_content: Which of the following is a spontaneous ovulator?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Cattle

Cattle are spontaneous ovulators — ovulation occurs automatically as part of the estrous cycle without requiring the stimulus of mating.

Spontaneous vs Induced Ovulation
  • Spontaneous ovulators: Ovulation is triggered by a natural pre-ovulatory LH surge independent of mating. Examples: Cattle, Buffalo, Mare, Sheep, Goat, Sow, Bitch
  • Induced (reflexive) ovulators: Ovulation is triggered only by coital stimulus → LH surge. Examples: Camel, Cat, Rabbit, Ferret, Mink, Llama
Why This Matters in Practice
  • In induced ovulators, AI must be accompanied by GnRH or hCG injection to induce ovulation, or timing must follow mating.
  • In spontaneous ovulators, ovulation time can be predicted from estrus onset and AI can be timed accordingly without hormonal intervention.

posts.post_title: Site of Fertilization – Birds vs Domestic Animals
posts.post_content: The site of fertilization in birds & domestic animals are respectively:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Infundibulum (Birds) & Ampulla/Ampullary-isthmic junction (Domestic Animals)

The site of fertilization differs between birds and domestic mammals:

  • Birds: Fertilization occurs in the Infundibulum — the most cranial/funnel-shaped part of the oviduct. The infundibulum picks up the ovulated yolk (ovum) from the ovary, and fertilization by stored sperm occurs here.
  • Domestic animals: Fertilization occurs at the Ampullary-isthmic junction of the oviduct (Fallopian tube) — where the ampulla (wider, convoluted part) meets the isthmus (narrower part).
Why the Difference?
  • In birds, the ovum is surrounded by yolk and albumen is added as it travels down — fertilization must occur BEFORE albumen and shell are added, hence at the very top (infundibulum).
  • In mammals, fertilization occurs in the oviduct at the ampullary-isthmic junction and the fertilized ovum then moves to the uterus for implantation.

posts.post_title: Cryogen and Cryoprotective Agent in Frozen Semen
posts.post_content: Most commonly used cryogen and cryoprotective agent in frozen semen are respectively:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: LN₂ and Glycerol

In frozen semen technology, Liquid Nitrogen (LN₂) is the most commonly used cryogen (the freezing agent/storage medium) and Glycerol is the most commonly used cryoprotective agent (CPA — protects sperm from freeze damage).

Role of Each
  • LN₂ (Liquid Nitrogen): Provides the ultra-low temperature environment (–196°C) for long-term storage. Inert, non-toxic to cells, and maintains temperature stably.
  • Glycerol: Penetrates sperm cell membrane and prevents intracellular ice crystal formation during freezing by depressing the freezing point and vitrifying the cytoplasm. Typically added at 6–7% concentration in bull semen extenders.
Other Cryoprotective Agents Used
  • DMSO (Dimethyl Sulfoxide) — used in some species
  • Ethylene glycol — used in vitrification protocols

posts.post_title: Source of PMSG Secretion
posts.post_content: PMSG is secreted by:

_aimcq_options.text: Both chorionic girdle and endometrial cups

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Both chorionic girdle and endometrial cups

PMSG (eCG) is secreted by both the chorionic girdle (the initial trophoblast invasion structure) and the endometrial cups (the established secretory structures formed after chorionic girdle invasion). These are sequential stages of the same foetal trophoblast-derived structure in mares.

Sequence of Events
  • Day 25: Chorionic girdle begins to form from the trophoblast
  • Day 36–38: Chorionic girdle cells invade the endometrium and form endometrial cups
  • Day 40: PMSG secretion begins
  • Day 60–70: Peak PMSG secretion
  • Day 120–150: Endometrial cups degenerate and PMSG disappears
Note

The fact that both structures are secretory sources is why the correct answer is 'Both'. In practice, endometrial cups are the primary, long-term secretory structures, while the chorionic girdle initiates the process.

posts.post_title: Cause of Fern Pattern in Cervical Mucus
posts.post_content: The fern pattern of cervical mucus is mainly due to:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: High sodium chloride (NaCl) content

The fern pattern (arborization/ferning) of cervical mucus when dried on a glass slide is due to the high sodium chloride (NaCl) content of the mucus during estrus. When estrogen levels peak (during heat), the cervical mucus becomes watery and rich in NaCl, which crystallizes into a characteristic fern-leaf pattern upon drying.

Ferning and the Estrous Cycle
  • During estrus: High estrogen → abundant, watery, acellular mucus with high NaCl → pronounced fern pattern
  • During luteal phase (diestrus): High progesterone → thick, viscous mucus with low NaCl → no fern pattern (beaded or granular pattern)
  • During pregnancy: No fern pattern (progesterone dominant)
Clinical Use

Ferning test is a simple, rapid, low-cost method to confirm estrus in cattle and other domestic animals before AI.

posts.post_title: Twinning as a Cause of Abortion – Species
posts.post_content: 'Twinning' is a very common cause of abortion in:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Mare

In the mare, twinning (twin pregnancy) is a very common cause of abortion. Unlike cattle where twin pregnancies sometimes proceed to term, the uterus of the mare cannot adequately support two fetuses, leading to abortion of both.

Why Twinning is Problematic in Mares
  • The mare has a T-shaped uterus with limited uterine capacity — not suited for two fetuses.
  • Twin pregnancies in mares lead to abortion (usually at 7–9 months), premature births, stillbirths, or birth of weak foals that die shortly after.
  • Management: Twins are routinely detected by ultrasound early and one vesicle is manually crushed (twin reduction) to save one pregnancy.
Contrast With Other Species
  • Sow: Litter-bearing animal — multiple fetuses are normal.
  • Bitch: Also litter-bearing — twinning is normal.
  • Sheep: Twins are common and usually well-tolerated.
  • Mare: Designed for singleton pregnancies — twinning is pathological ✔

posts.post_title: Sigmoid Flexure Absent – Species
posts.post_content: Sigmoid flexure is absent in:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Both Stallion and Dog

The sigmoid (S-shaped) flexure is a curve in the non-erect penis that straightens during erection. It is absent in both the stallion and the dog — these species have musculocavernous (vascular) type penises that rely primarily on blood engorgement for erection.

Penis Types in Domestic Animals
  • Fibroelastic type (with sigmoid flexure): Bull, Ram, Buck, Boar, Camel — the penis is rigid even when non-erect; erection mainly involves straightening of the sigmoid flexure.
  • Musculocavernous (vascular) type (no sigmoid flexure): Stallion, Dog — penis enlarges greatly due to blood engorgement. ✔
Location of Sigmoid Flexure
  • Pre-scrotal (in front of scrotum): Boar, Camel
  • Post-scrotal (behind scrotum): Bull, Ram, Buck

posts.post_title: Site of Fertilization in Cattle
posts.post_content: The site of fertilization in cattle is:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Ampullary-isthmic junction

In cattle (and all domestic animals), fertilization occurs at the Ampullary-isthmic junction (AIJ) — the junction between the ampulla (wider, upper portion) and the isthmus (narrower, lower portion) of the oviduct (Fallopian tube).

Why Fertilization Occurs at AIJ
  • Spermatozoa, after being deposited in the cervix during AI or natural mating, migrate upward through the uterus and into the oviduct — the isthmus acts as a sperm reservoir.
  • The ovulated oocyte, swept into the oviduct by the infundibulum, moves down the ampulla.
  • Sperm released from the isthmus reservoir meet the oocyte at the ampullary-isthmic junction.
Post-Fertilization Journey
  • Fertilized ovum → zygote → cleaves as it moves down the oviduct → enters uterus as morula/blastocyst → implants in endometrium.

posts.post_title: Effect Similar to PMSG
posts.post_content: The effect of PMSG (Pregnant Mare Serum Gonadotropin) is similar to:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: FSH

PMSG (Pregnant Mare Serum Gonadotropin), also known as eCG (Equine Chorionic Gonadotropin), has a biological effect predominantly similar to FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone). It promotes follicular development and is widely used for superovulation protocols in cattle and sheep.

Comparison: PMSG vs. hCG
  • PMSG (eCG): FSH-like effect → follicle growth and superovulation
  • hCG (Human Chorionic Gonadotropin): LH-like effect → ovulation induction
Half-life Comparison
  • PMSG has the longest half-life of all gonadotropins (~6 days), due to its very high sialic acid content.
  • Half-life order: PMSG > hCG > FSH > LH > Oxytocin
Use in Superovulation

PMSG + hCG combination is used in embryo transfer programs: PMSG stimulates multiple follicle development (FSH action), then hCG triggers their ovulation (LH action).

posts.post_title: Match the Column: Hormones and Their Secretory Sources
posts.post_content:
Match the column — Hormones and their secretory sources:

2. Progesterone(b) Sertoli cell

5. Anti-Mullerian hormone(e) Anterior pituitary

Correct Answer: 1-d, 2-f, 3-g, 4-e, 5-b, 6-a, 7-c

The correct matching of hormones with their secretory organs:

  • Estrogen: Theca interna cells of Graafian follicle (in females); also Sertoli cells in males in small amounts
  • Progesterone: Corpus luteum (primary source)
  • Testosterone: Leydig cells (interstitial cells of testes)
  • Prolactin: Anterior pituitary (mammotroph cells)

  • Epinephrine (Adrenaline): Adrenal medulla
  • Renin: Kidney (juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney)
Clinical Note on AMH

AMH inhibits the development of Mullerian (paramesonephric) duct in male embryos, causing regression of the female reproductive tract precursor. Its serum level is also used as a marker of ovarian reserve in females.

posts.post_title: Physiological State Indicated by Fern Pattern
posts.post_content: The fern pattern of cervical mucus reflects that the animal is in:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Heat (Estrus)

The fern/arborization pattern in cervical mucus is a reliable indicator that the animal is in heat (estrus). During estrus, peak estrogen levels cause profound changes in cervical mucus composition — it becomes clear, watery, and abundant with a high NaCl content, which produces the distinctive fern-leaf crystallization pattern when dried and viewed under a microscope.

How to Perform the Ferning Test
  1. Collect a small sample of cervical mucus using a swab or gloved finger.
  2. Spread a thin film on a clean glass slide.
  3. Allow to air-dry completely (3–5 minutes).
  4. Examine under low-power microscope (10x).
Interpretation
  • Positive (fern pattern present): Animal is in estrus — good time for AI
  • Negative (no fern pattern): Animal is in diestrus or pregnant — not in heat

posts.post_title: Disease Prevented by AI with Frozen Semen
posts.post_content: By Artificial insemination (A.I.) with frozen semen, which of the following disease can be prevented?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Vibriosis (Campylobacteriosis)

Vibriosis (caused by Campylobacter fetus subsp. venerealis) is a venereal disease transmitted only through natural mating (coitus). Because AI with frozen semen eliminates the physical contact between bull and cow, Vibriosis can be prevented through AI.

Why AI Prevents Vibriosis Specifically
  • C. fetus subsp. venerealis lives in the prepuce/sheath of the bull and is transmitted to the cow's reproductive tract during natural service.
  • With AI, no physical contact occurs — the organism cannot be transmitted.
  • Similarly, Trichomoniasis (caused by Tritrichomonas foetus) is also a venereal disease preventable by AI.
Diseases NOT Prevented by AI
  • IBR: Transmitted via respiratory secretions and nasal contact — not a venereal route.
  • FMD: Highly contagious via aerosol, contact, fomites — AI does not prevent spread.
Key Rule

AI with frozen semen prevents venereal diseases (Vibriosis & Trichomoniasis) because it eliminates bull-cow genital contact. Answer here is Vibriosis as the single-best option listed.

posts.post_title: Proestrus Bleeding – Species
posts.post_content: Proestrus bleeding occurs in:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Bitch

Proestrus bleeding (serosanguineous vulvar discharge) is a characteristic feature of the bitch. It occurs during proestrus (the phase before true estrus/heat) due to estrogenic stimulation of the uterine endometrium causing diapedesis of red blood cells.

Key Points
  • Proestrus in the bitch lasts approximately 9 days, during which the bloody discharge is present.
  • The bitch is NOT in true standing heat during proestrus — she may attract males but will NOT stand for mating.
  • True standing heat (estrus) begins when the discharge becomes lighter/straw-colored and she accepts mounting.
Comparison: Types of Bleeding in Domestic Animals
  • Proestrus bleeding: Bitch ✔ (before estrus)
  • Metestrus bleeding (post-estrus): Cattle — occurs 1–2 days after end of estrus due to withdrawal of estrogen causing uterine capillary rupture.

posts.post_title: Type & Shape of Uterus in She-Camel
posts.post_content: Type and shape of the uterus in she-camel is:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Bicornuate, between T & Y shape

The uterus of the she-camel is classified as bicornuate in type and has a shape that is between T and Y — intermediate between the T-shape of the mare and the Y-shape of ruminants.

Uterine Classifications Summary
  • Type — Bicornuate: Sow, She-camel (two horns, shared uterine body, no septum)
  • Type — Bipartite: Cow, Mare, Ewe (two horns joined with partial septum or common body)
  • Type — Duplex: Rodents (two completely separate uteri)
Shape of Uterus
  • Y-shape: Ruminants (cattle, sheep, goat)
  • T-shape: Mare
  • Between T and Y: She-camel ✔
Special Feature of She-Camel Uterus

Despite having two horns, approximately 99% of pregnancies in the she-camel are confined to the left horn.

posts.post_title: Effect Similar to hCG
posts.post_content: The effect of hCG (Human Chorionic Gonadotropin) is similar to:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: LH

hCG (Human Chorionic Gonadotropin) has an effect predominantly similar to LH (Luteinizing Hormone). It binds to LH receptors and triggers ovulation of mature follicles and luteinization of granulosa cells.

Clinical Uses of hCG
  • Ovulation induction: hCG is injected to trigger ovulation of a dominant follicle in embryo transfer and timed AI programs.
  • Treatment of cystic ovarian disease (COD): especially follicular cysts in cattle.
  • Treatment of subestrus/silent heat in cattle.
Comparison: PMSG vs. hCG
  • PMSG: FSH-like → follicle stimulation/superovulation
  • hCG: LH-like → ovulation trigger, luteinization
Half-life of hCG

hCG has a half-life of about 11 hours, which is longer than LH (~60 minutes) but shorter than PMSG (~6 days).

posts.post_title: Water-Soluble Glycoprotein Ovarian Hormone
posts.post_content: Which of the following ovarian hormones is glycoprotein in nature and soluble in water?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Relaxin

Relaxin is the only ovarian hormone that is a glycoprotein in nature and is therefore water-soluble. It belongs to the insulin-like peptide family.

Chemical Nature of Ovarian Hormones
  • Estrogen (Estradiol): Steroid hormone — lipid-soluble, derived from cholesterol
  • Progesterone: Steroid hormone — lipid-soluble, derived from cholesterol
  • Androgen (Testosterone): Steroid hormone — lipid-soluble
  • Relaxin: Glycoprotein (peptide) — water-soluble ✔
Function of Relaxin
  • Softening and relaxation of pelvic ligaments and the pubic symphysis in preparation for parturition
  • Relaxation of the cervix for dilation during labour
  • Inhibition of uterine contractions during pregnancy
  • In females, secreted by the corpus luteum (especially in dogs and pigs), placenta, and uterus

posts.post_title: Predominant Horn of Pregnancy in Cattle and Camel
posts.post_content: Most of the pregnancies in cattle and camel are located respectively in:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Right horn (cattle) and Left horn (camel)

In cattle, approximately 60% of pregnancies occur in the right uterine horn (due to the higher proportion of right-side ovulations from the right ovary being functionally dominant in most cycles). In the she-camel, the opposite is true — 99% of pregnancies are in the left uterine horn (the left ovary is functionally dominant in camels).

Summary by Species
  • Cattle: ~60% right horn (right ovary more active)
  • She-camel: 99% left horn (left ovary dominant)
  • Mare: No significant horn preference
Practical Implication

During rectal palpation for pregnancy diagnosis in cattle, the examiner typically checks the right horn first. In camels, a pregnancy found in the right horn is unusual and the clinician should investigate for anatomical anomalies.
